- `find` / recursive `ls` to locate files by name pattern → `Glob` (plain `ls <known-directory>` is fine for listing a directory)
- `grep` / `rg` (search file contents) → `Grep`
- `echo` / `printf` (talk to the user) → just output text directly

The dedicated tools render in the per-tool permission UI and keep raw stdout out of the conversation; that is why they are worth reaching for whenever one fits.

**Output:**
The stdout and stderr will be combined and returned as a string. The output may be truncated if it is too long. If the command exits non-zero, the output ends with a `Command failed with exit code: N` line; a command killed by its timeout or interrupted by the user ends with its own message instead.

Background execution is disabled for this agent. Do not set `run_in_background=true`.

**Guidelines for safety and security:**
- Each shell tool call will be executed in a fresh shell environment. The shell variables, current working directory changes, and the shell history is not preserved between calls. To run a command in a particular directory, pass the `cwd` argument (or use absolute paths) rather than relying on a `cd` from an earlier call.
- The tool call will return after the command is finished. You shall not use this tool to execute an interactive command or a command that may run forever. For possibly long-running commands, set the `timeout` argument in seconds. The default is 60s; foreground commands allow up to 300s; a foreground command that hits its timeout is killed.
- Avoid using `..` to access files or directories outside of the working directory.
- Avoid modifying files outside of the working directory unless explicitly instructed to do so.
- Never run commands that require superuser privileges unless explicitly instructed to do so.

- Use `&&` to chain commands that genuinely depend on each other, e.g. `npm install && npm test`. tools.description:
Find files by glob pattern, sorted by modification time (most recent first).

Powered by ripgrep. Respects `.gitignore`, `.ignore`, and `.rgignore` by default — set `include_ignored` to also match ignored files (e.g. build outputs, `node_modules`). Sensitive files (such as `.env`) are always filtered out. Matches are files only — directories themselves are never listed; to find a directory, glob for a file inside it (e.g. `**/fixtures/**`).

Good patterns:
- `*.ts` — all files matching an extension, at any depth below the search root (a bare pattern without `/` matches recursively)
- `src/*.ts` — files directly inside `src/` (one level, not recursive)
- `src/**/*.ts` — recursive walk with a subdirectory anchor and extension
- `**/*.py` — recursive walk from the search root for an extension
- `*.{ts,tsx}` — brace expansion is supported

# Quotes Highlighter — Behavioral Spec (tailspin v5.6.0)

## 1. Exact ANSI styling (default config)

- Quote span: `ESC[33m` + matched text (including the quote characters) + `ESC[0m`
- That is plain yellow foreground (SGR 33), **no bold/italic/underline**, and the **opening quote, content, and closing quote are all one single styled span** — there is no separate styling for the delimiters vs. the content, and no inner separators.
- Reset is a full `ESC[0m`, emitted immediately after the closing quote. Adjacent spans each get their own open/reset: `"a""b"` → `^[[33m"a"^[[0m^[[33m"b"^[[0m`.
- Style is themeable: `[quotes.style] fg = "red"` in a theme TOML produces `^[[31m…^[[0m`; adding `bold = true` produces `^[[1;31m…^[[0m` (attribute codes precede color, `;`-joined). The `quotes` table only confirmed field is `style` (struct Style with at least `fg`, `bold`); unknown keys are silently ignored.

## 2. Match rules

- **Only the double-quote character `"` is a quote delimiter. Single quotes `'` and backticks `` ` `` are never highlighted** (verified with the group isolated and in full default config: `it's a 'single' quote test` → no highlight at all, apostrophes harmless).
- Equivalent regex per line: **`"[^"]*"`** (global, non-overlapping, left-to-right), i.e. a `"`, any run of non-`"` chars (may be empty, may contain tabs, punctuation, Unicode, spaces — everything except `"`), then the next `"`. Pairs are strictly sequential: quote #1 pairs with #2, #3 with #4, etc. No nesting concept, no escape handling (`\` is an ordinary char and `\"` counts as a quote char).
- **Line-wide parity gate (the big surprise): if the total count of `"` characters on the line is odd, NO quote highlighting is applied anywhere on that line** — even complete pairs already present are left plain. (Equivalently: the whole line must match `^(?:[^"]|"[^"]*")*$` for any quote span to be emitted.)
- The gate is per line: an odd line does not affect neighboring lines.
- Empty string `""` matches (zero-width content). A lone `"`, `"unterminated`, or `trailing"` yield nothing.

## 3. Boundary / edge cases (input → exact output, flags `--enable quotes --disable-builtin-keywords`)

- `hello "world" end` → `hello ^[[33m"world"^[[0m end`
- `empty "" quotes` → `empty ^[[33m""^[[0m quotes`
- `word"inside"word` → `word^[[33m"inside"^[[0mword` (no word-boundary requirement)
- `("paren"),["bracket"]."dot",` → each quoted span highlighted, adjacent punctuation untouched
- `a\t"tab\there"\tz` → `a<TAB>^[[33m"tab<TAB>here"^[[0m<TAB>z` (tabs inside spans fine)
- `é"café"x` → `é^[[33m"café"^[[0mx` (Unicode inert)
- `say "he said \"hi\"" ok` → `say ^[[33m"he said \"^[[0mhi\^[[33m""^[[0m ok` — **escapes are not understood**: the `\"` closes the first span; remaining `"…"` re-pair sequentially
- `unmatched "quote`, `x "a" y " `, `"a" "b" "c" "d" "e` (odd count) → **completely plain output**
- `"a" "b" "c" "d"` (even) → all four spans highlighted
- `a"b"c"d` → plain (it's 3 quotes — odd; easy to miscount)
- `a "b"` + `\r\n` line ending → `a^[[33m"b"^[[0m^M` (CR passes through outside the span)

## 4. Precedence quirk (interaction with other highlighters)

When another highlighter's span falls inside a quoted span, the **entire quote span is discarded** (not trimmed) and only the inner match is styled; the quote characters render plain:

- `pre "123" post` with quotes+numbers → `pre "^[[36m123^[[0m" post`
- `x "true" y` with builtin keywords → `x "^[[3;31mtrue^[[0m" y`
- `x "ERROR msg" y` (default config) → `x "^[[31mERROR^[[0m msg" y`

Order of `--enable` flags doesn't matter — precedence is internal and fixed (numbers and builtin keywords outrank quotes). Numbers use `ESC[36m` (cyan); `true` uses `ESC[3;31m` (italic red), `ERROR` uses `ESC[31m`.

Exit code is 0 and stderr empty in all normal cases. Config-file parse errors print an `Error:` diagnostic to stderr but still exit 0 (no output).

## Implementation pseudocode

```python
def highlight_quotes(line):           # line = one line without trailing \n
    if line.count('"') % 2 == 1:
        return line                    # parity gate: bail out entirely
    return re.sub(r'"[^"]*"', lambda m: "\x1b[33m" + m.group(0) + "\x1b[0m", line)
```

Apply this only where no higher-precedence span (numbers, keywords, etc.) overlaps the quote span; on overlap, drop the quote span wholesale.
